title: Lock out an equipment cord with a plug lockout and padlock
instruction: Lock out the cord with the yellow tag: unplug it from the outlet, lay its plug in the open red plug lockout with the cord through the notch at its end, close the lid, then put the blue padlock's shackle through both tabs and snap it shut. Leave the cord with the green tag plugged in.
context: Cord-and-plug equipment is isolated for servicing by unplugging it; a plug lockout keeps the plug under the worker's padlock so nobody plugs the machine back in while their hands are in it. Unplugging the wrong cord stops a machine someone else is relying on, and a lockout box that is shut but not padlocked can simply be opened.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Outlet: a light-grey 3 mm steel plate (20 cm wide, 21.75 cm tall) stands upright on the table, fixed to it, its front face 33.3 cm in front of the bases, spanning 7 to 27 cm right of the midline. A duplex NEMA 5-15R receptacle (15 A 125 V, ivory, ground holes down, stainless cover plate 7 x 11.5 cm) is mounted in it centred 17 cm right of the midline; its two outlet faces stand 3 mm proud of the plate, the top outlet's blade slots centred 17.75 cm above the table, the bottom outlet's 13.85 cm. Cords: two black 16/3 SJT cords (8 mm across, about 0.1 kg/m), each 60 cm long with a molded NEMA 5-15P plug (black, body 38 mm wide, 30 mm tall and 30 mm long plus an 18 mm strain relief, 50 g), one plugged fully into each outlet. Each cord leaves its plug toward the robot, drops to the table and runs to a cord clamp screwed to the table: the top cord's clamp 10 cm in front of the bases and 40 cm right of the midline, the bottom cord's 22 cm in front and 43 cm right (the paths in the setup photo). Each cord carries a flag tag (4.5 x 2.2 cm) 5 to 7.5 cm from its plug: yellow, printed GRINDER, on the top cord; green, printed VENT FAN, on the bottom cord. Lockout: a red Brady 65674 plug lockout (polypropylene; two half-shells 8.9 cm long, 5.1 cm wide and 2.55 cm deep with 2.5 mm walls, hinged along one long edge; at one end a 12.7 mm cord hole split between the two halves; on the free edge at mid-length each half has a 3 mm thick, 2.4 cm square tab with a 9.5 mm hole 1.35 cm out from the shell) lies open like a book on a grey steel stand. Its lower half lies cavity up, long axis left-right from 0.45 cm left to 8.45 cm right of the midline, front edge 19 cm in front of the bases, rim 15.25 cm above the table, cord notch at its right end and tab toward the robot; two clips on the stand hold its back corners. The lid lies open flat behind it, hinged along the lower half's back edge 24.1 cm in front of the bases. Stand: a grey steel block 10 cm deep, 12 cm wide and 12.67 cm tall, spanning 19.55 to 29.6 cm in front of the bases and 2 cm left to 10 cm right of the midline. Padlock: a blue Master Lock 410BLU Zenex padlock (thermoplastic body 38 x 19 x 44 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle, 38 mm vertical clearance, 100 g), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, lies on its 38 x 44 mm face, shackle pointing right toward the lockout's tab and tilted 15 degrees down, its body centred 13 cm in front of the bases and 8 cm left of the midline, on a grey steel pedestal (a 1.2 x 1.6 cm column on a 5 x 5 x 1 cm foot) whose 3.8 x 2.2 cm top slopes 15 degrees down toward the lockout, from 12.15 to 11.6 cm above the table, and carries only the shackle end of the body (the other end overhangs it). Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if the green-tagged plug is pulled 3 mm or more out of its outlet at any time. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached. 0.25: the yellow-tagged plug is unplugged (its front 2 cm or more from the outlet face, so the ground pin is clear). 0.5: the whole plug, blades and strain relief included, lies inside the lockout's lower half (inside the space the two shells enclose when shut, within 1 mm). 0.75: the lid is shut (within 3 degrees of closed) with the plug inside. 1.0: the padlock's shackle is snapped shut through both tabs' holes with the lid shut on the plug, and the after-release check passes. After-release check, once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock and 7 cm from the lockout's centre for 1 s (if they never are, the check is not done and the score is at most 0.75): (1) hook a spring scale in the lid's tab and pull it up with 8 N (0.5 N m about the hinge) for 1.5 s: passes if the lid opens less than 10 degrees; (2) holding the lockout's lower half, pull the cord straight out of the cord hole with 40 N on a spring scale for 1.5 s: passes if the plug stays wholly inside. A padlocked lockout that fails either check stays at 0.75. Angles are read from a photo with a protractor; distances with a rule.
reset_notes: Unlock the padlock with its key, take it off the tabs, close its shackle to the popped-up position and lay it back on the pedestal, shackle toward the lockout. Open the lockout, take the plug out and push it fully back into the top outlet, lay its cord back along its starting path (setup photo) and lay the lid open flat. Check that the green-tagged plug is fully in. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, station arm gains. Geometry holds: the 38 x 30 mm plug cannot pass the 12.7 mm cord hole; a shackle through both tabs stops the lid. Published: lockout size, cord hole, NEMA blades, 410 outline. Inferred: shell walls, tab size, plug body. Rules: outlet grip is a spring (5 N, below real), shackle latch; cords are capsule chains; tags visual; lower half fixed; check applied after recording. Details in README.
